editorial:
Imagine finding an old car in the woods with a man inside who passed away a long time ago, and right next to him is his dog who stayed by his side until the very end. It sounds sad, but the movie turns this into a beautiful story about loyalty. You follow a city worker named Kyousuke as he tries to figure out who the man was so he can give him a proper burial. As he digs into the man's past, the movie shifts to show you the world through the dog's eyes. It feels very cozy and quiet, focusing on the deep bond between a pet and its owner in a way that really hits home.

What makes this one special is how it handles grief without feeling too heavy. The acting is natural, and the slow pace lets you really feel the emotions. If you have ever loved a pet, you will probably cry, so keep some tissues nearby. It is a slow burn, so if you want a loud action movie, this isn't it. However, for a quiet night in, you should definitely try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or renting it on Apple TV to see the beautiful scenery. It is a great pick for a rainy Sunday.
endingExplained: You find out the man was lonely and struggling, but his dog was his entire world. The dog stayed in the car for months, refusing to leave his owner's side even after he died. This ultimate act of love touches Kyousuke, helping him heal from the loss of his own family. The movie ends with the man and dog finally getting peace, leaving you with a warm feeling about true friendship.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about animals and loyalty.
